text:
alex: heads up — apiserver error rate jumped in eu-west at 08:10 UTC, controller-manager reconcile backlog climbing and a ton of GPU attach failures reported by the provisioner. anyone oncall?

sasha: i'm on it. seeing a spike of 'context deadline exceeded' from the attach controller and apiserver 5xx spikes. kubelet logs show a bunch of ephemeral fd errors on node-gpu-*-eu1.

munir: i pulled controller-manager logs: 
```
E0319 08:10:12.345 reconcile.go:212] attach failed: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded
W0319 08:10:12.346 controller.go:98] reconcile backlog length=1420
```

alex: thanks — can you also check apiserver metrics (inflight requests, file descriptors)? thinking this might be a fanout + slow kvstore combo.

ops-bot: alert muted for 30m by sasha (reason: investigating). :information_source:

jenna: i see etcd latencies increased around same time: 95th p99 wrote to disk spike ~380ms, snapshot IO concurrently running in eu-west snapshotter-job.

munir: here's quick command to snapshot metrics and current pods on kube-system: 
```
kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide --kubeconfig=/etc/kube/kubeconfig
curl -sS 'http://apiserver:9090/metrics' | grep apiserver_request_duration_seconds_bucket
```

alex: good call. digging into provisioner — there's a burst of GPU attach requests after a scheduled job started scaling. provisioner attempted parallel attaches beyond driver limit and we started seeing attach timeouts that cascade into controller-manager retries which amplify apiserver load.

sasha: posting kernel logs from one node (truncated): 
```
Mar 19 08:09:58 node-gpu-12 kernel: nvme0: I/O 1234 timeout
Mar 19 08:10:01 node-gpu-12 kubelet: E0320 08:10:01 kubelet_volumes.go:195] Unable to attach volume: fd allocation failed: too many open files
```

jenna: is this limited to a single availability zone or cross-zone? cost/team note: if we push more reserved instances to avoid cold attach storms we pay more, but rolling throttles hurt job latency.

alex: initial triage: 1) reduce attachment concurrency on provisioner to 2x driver-safe parallelism 2) temporarily pause snapshotter-job in eu-west to give etcd breathing room 3) increase apiserver ulimit for fd to 65k 4) add backpressure metric and alert for attach_retries > 50/min.

munir: i'm patching the provisioner config now (setting max_parallel_attaches=8 -> 4) and restarting a single replica. will watch.

sasha: i'm taking snapshotter-job down for 10m. ops-bot: runbook step applied -> scale snapshotter-job to 0 in eu-west.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: provisioner config patch rolled to one replica (image: provisioner:v2.4.1-hotfix). :rocket:

jenna: can we also temporarily enable apiserver rate-limiter to cap unauthenticated/list watch fanout? saw a noisy job doing lots of list calls.

alex: yes, enabling the list watch qps cap to 30. doing a quick apiserver restart on one leader to pick up ulimit bump after verifying PID namespace perms.

munir: monitoring: controller-manager backlog dropped from 1420 -> 180 in 12m after the provisioner patch and snapshotter pause. apiserver 5xx rate fell back to baseline.

sasha: confirmed fd usage on node-gpu-12 decreased from 61k -> 9k after the restart and driver stabilised.

jenna: follow-ups: - permanent config: adaptive attach throttling based on node driver health - improve driver telemetry and exporter for attach latency - evaluate scheduled snapshotter windows to avoid control plane heavy periods - cost tradeoff doc for reserving more warm capacity vs. on-demand throttles

alex: leaving a concise incident note in postmortems channel after we validate no regressions. nice quick loop everyone. :thumbsup:
